summary.headline: Phoenix Mills Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to Rs 1,075 crore and operating EBITDA 14% to Rs 642 crore, with retail consumption up 32%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs 1,075 crore and operating EBITDA grew 14% to Rs 642 crore at a 60% margin, with net profit up 23% to Rs 297 crore. Core annuity revenue rose 17% to Rs 1,033 crore and core EBITDA rose 19% to Rs 649 crore. Retail consumption grew 32% to Rs 4,730 crore, though jewelry and electronics drove much of that growth; ex-jewelry and electronics consumption grew 24% while rental grew 17%. Capex was Rs 1,085 crore, including Rs 716 crore paid to GAMADA for Chandigarh land, and net debt stood at Rs 3,658 crore (1.3x net debt/EBITDA).

financial_highlights.metric: Operating free cash flow (net of interest and tax)
financial_highlights.value: Rs 602 crore; core businesses Rs 584 crore
Rs 5,658 crore / Rs 3,658 crore; net debt/EBITDA 1.3x

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Rental income Rs 594 crore (+17%) and EBITDA Rs 625 crore (+17%); consumption Rs 4,730 crore (+32%), ex-jewelry and electronics +24%. Apparel and accessories (60% of trading area) +24%, jewelry +55%, electronics +61%, F&B and entertainment combined above 20%.

segments.name: Offices
segments.commentary: Income Rs 75 crore (+44% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 42 crore (+31% YoY). Leased occupancy 72% (June 2026) vs 70% a year earlier; rent-paying occupancy 42%, targeted to converge with leased occupancy by March 2027.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Income Rs 145 crore (+18% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 62 crore (+19% YoY); St. Regis Mumbai income +19% and EBITDA +20%.

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Q1 booking Rs 64 crore and collection Rs 51 crore; about 1.5 lakh sq ft completed inventory unsold at OBW and Kessaku. About Rs 84 crore of sales (incl. Rs 20 crore carried over) expected to reflect in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Retail rental income guided to mid-teens growth for both FY27 and FY28, reiterated on the call.
Consumption: July 2026 trending above 20% growth; management expects healthy double-digit consumption growth going forward; September is seasonally the weakest month.
Retail rent-to-consumption ratio to be maintained in a 12% to 14% range (currently about 12.5%).

New openings in FY27-FY28: Phoenix Grand Victoria (Kolkata, about 1 million sq ft), Phoenix Surat (about 1 million sq ft, now end-2027 or early 2028), Phoenix Palladium expansion (about 4.5 lakh sq ft, FY27/FY28, about 50% leased), Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore Phase-2 (about 170,000 sq ft F&B floor, early 2027), Whitefield offices (about 0.4 million sq ft) and 400-key Grand Hyatt.
Offices: leased occupancy targeted at 90% by end FY27 for Phoenix Asia Towers and One National Park Chennai.
Residential launches in Kolkata and Bengaluru by end 2026 or early 2027; Kolkata about 1.2 million sq ft at a launch price around Rs 30,000 per sq ft (approximate).
Lower Parel Project Rise pre-leasing under way at Rs 350 to 400 per sq ft on leasable area; combined Rise office and adjacent tower 1.5 to 1.6 million sq ft.
Retail platform targeted at 18 million sq ft by 2030; Thane, Chandigarh and Coimbatore completions targeted by 2030.
risks_watch: Consumption growth is heavily dependent on jewelry and electronics and gold prices; a fall could slow headline consumption.
Rent-to-consumption ratio has fallen from about 14% three years ago to about 12.5% this quarter; management guides 12% to 14%.
Surat and Kolkata openings slipping into end-2027 or early 2028, and Palladium expansion timing (FY27/FY28), are execution items.
Office rent-paying occupancy at 42% must converge toward 72% leased occupancy by March 2027.
Residential launch timelines (Kolkata and Bengaluru) described as indicative; pace of inventory sell-down (1.5 lakh sq ft unsold).
September consumption seasonally weakest; Q2 consumption outcome is the next checkpoint.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operating momentum and leasing, with cautious qualifiers on the timing of new openings and on gold-linked consumption. Management was evasive on the anchor-level split of expiries and avoided giving a firm launch date for Surat, Kolkata residential and Lower Parel plans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Bengaluru residential and Kolkata launch now pushed to early 2027, and what product and price for Kolkata?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timelines are indicative, driven by approvals and RERA rather than delay; Bengaluru sold at about Rs 36,000 per sq ft in Q1. Kolkata is about 1.2 million sq ft at around Rs 30,000 per sq ft, a premium gated community.

qa_highlights.question: Will fashion rental growth catch up to the 24% consumption growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 50% of the portfolio expiring over three years and said rental growth will come from renewals, new assets and revenue share; partnership model means no maximisation of short-term rent. Non-gold consumption +24% vs rent +17%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 8.7 million sq ft expiry is anchors and what is the mark-to-market upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not provide the anchor breakup and avoided guidance on mark-to-market; past expiries have driven rental growth of 20% to 30%. Mall of Asia reached Rs 3,000 per sq ft trading density within three years.

qa_highlights.question: Lower Parel: pre-leasing status, rates, and timing of development plan for the extra FSI?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-leasing has started with some area committed at Rs 350 to 400 per sq ft on leasable area. Development plans for the additional FSI to be shared after Rise Retail opens; approvals partly secured.

qa_highlights.question: Jewelry and electronics contribution to rental income, and gold price exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Jewelry and electronics are about 5% of trading area, 28% of consumption and about 7.5% of rental income; management acknowledged jewelry growth partly reflects higher gold prices that may reverse.

qa_highlights.question: Surat timing and rental contribution from FY28 openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat expected by end-2027 or early 2028, launch date to be fixed by mid-next year. Fixed rent starts from first month of tenant trading; malls take about 12 months to reach 85% to 90% occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Consumption outlook after July and rent-to-consumption trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: July trending above 20%; September weakest month. Rent-to-consumption expected in 12% to 14% range, currently about 12.5%; mid-teens rental growth guided for FY27 and FY28.

capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex Rs 1,085 crore: Rs 314 crore construction and Rs 771 crore land acquisition and development rights, mainly Rs 716 crore balance payment to GAMADA for Chandigarh land; Chandigarh now wholly owned by PML and excavation has started.

Retail pipeline: Phoenix Grand Victoria (Kolkata, about 1 million sq ft) and Phoenix Surat (about 1 million sq ft, end-2027 or early 2028), Phoenix Palladium expansion (about 4.5 lakh sq ft, FY27/FY28, about 50% leased), Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore Phase-2 (F&B floor about 170,000 sq ft, early 2027, 30-plus restaurants).

Offices: Whitefield Bengaluru about 0.4 million sq ft and 400-key Grand Hyatt in Whitefield; Whitefield Phase-3 approvals secured, civil work to start shortly. Lower Parel Project Rise plus adjacent tower 1.5 to 1.6 million sq ft; pre-leasing started at Rs 350 to 400 per sq ft on leasable area.

Residential: Kolkata about 1.2 million sq ft, launch price around Rs 30,000 per sq ft (indicative); Bengaluru launch by end-2026 or early 2027, Q1 average realisation about Rs 36,000 per sq ft. Thane total potential over 4 million sq ft (1.3 million sq ft mall, about 400-key hotel, 1.2 million sq ft office); Chandigarh mall 1.5 to 1.7 million sq ft.

Capacity: retail platform targeted at 18 million sq ft by 2030; Thane, Chandigarh and Coimbatore completions targeted by 2030. Office platform about 5 million sq ft across Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru and Chennai versus about 2 million sq ft in 2024.
demand_pricing: Consumption Rs 4,730 crore, +32% YoY; ex-jewelry and electronics +24%; trading density +26%. Apparel and accessories (60% of trading area) +24%, jewelry +55%, electronics +61%, F&B and entertainment combined above 20%, F&B alone +26% in the rest-of-portfolio view.

Jewelry and electronics occupy about 5% of trading area, contribute 28% of consumption and about 7.5% of rental income; productivity about 5 times portfolio average. Rest of portfolio (~70%) consumption +24%, rental +17%.
July 2026 consumption trending above 20% growth; management expects healthy double-digit consumption growth going forward; September seasonally weakest month.
Rental income Rs 594 crore (+17%); rent-to-consumption about 12.5%, down from about 14% three years ago; management guides 12% to 14%. Mid-teens rental growth guided for FY27 and FY28.

Leasing: over 300 transactions covering nearly 1 million sq ft in Q1; about 390 new stores in last 12 months; malls leased at 97% to 98%; Phoenix MarketCity Pune (Avenue of Stars) consumption +29%, Bengaluru consumption +22%, both at 89% trading occupancy. About 50% of portfolio up for lease expiry over next three years (8.7 million sq ft over five years cited by analyst); anchor split not disclosed.

Offices: leased occupancy 72% (June 2026) vs 70% a year earlier; rent-paying occupancy 42%, expected to converge to leased occupancy by March 2027. Residential Q1 bookings Rs 64 crore, collections Rs 51 crore; about 1.5 lakh sq ft completed inventory unsold at OBW and Kessaku; Rs 84 crore sales (incl. Rs 20 crore carried over) expected in Q2.
key_quotes: So, total Rs. 84 crore sales is likely to reflect in Q2 which has already been done till 30th June.
And how you do in that month actually makes or breaks your consumption numbers for the quarter.
The important point to note is that consumption does not translate into rental income one-on-one.
Importantly this means we are now developing Chandigarh as a wholly owned project of PML and we have just started excavation work to this site.

growth.why: Management reiterated mid-teens retail rental growth for FY27 and FY28 and healthy double-digit consumption growth (July trending above 20%), backed by named mall openings (Surat, Palladium expansion, MarketCity Bangalore Phase-2) and 89% occupancy at Pune and Bengaluru, though most new capacity lands 2-4 quarters out and the Rs 1,075 crore consolidated revenue rose 13%.
